observations.text: SP, at the level expected for this block, flew the published instrument departure with the IP directing the initial radial intercept and the first crossing restriction; course deviation reached 10 degrees from the departure radial before the correction was directed. Track deviations were recognized only after the IP identified them. Performance was at the desired code but marginal for the Training Section - independent execution of the MAIP departure sequence, with earlier recognition of track deviations, is expected to improve.

SP, on a first exposure to the published instrument departure, flew the SID sequence to completion using the IP's verbal prompts for the turn point and the crossing altitude, without any control input by the IP. Course deviation from the departure radial peaked at 8 degrees and was corrected after the prompt. ATC instructions were read back correctly and complied with. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the published instrument departure as described in the MAIP without IP prompting, holding the departure radial with two excursions of 6 to 7 degrees. Both track deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, and the crossing restriction was met. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the published instrument departure in accordance with the MAIP and the Basic Control Standards, without IP assistance. Course deviation from the departure radial did not exceed 3 degrees, and each deviation was corrected promptly. All ATC instructions were read back correctly and complied with. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew the published instrument departure and executed it flawlessly, without IP assistance and within the Basic Control Standards. Course deviation from the departure radial remained within 1 degree throughout the climb and the crossing restrictions were met with negligible error. ATC instructions were anticipated, read back and complied with immediately. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an unstructured radial intercept technique that used bank angle instead of a computed intercept heading, did not establish the aircraft on the published departure radial at the turn point. Course deviation reached 14 degrees and continued to increase, with the result that the IP directed the intercept heading and flew part of the climb segment. Further study of the MAIP departure plate and of the intercept procedure is required.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not set the departure course and did not comply with the ATC climb instruction. Course deviation from the published radial exceeded 12 degrees and the crossing restriction was missed, with the result that the IP took control and re-established the aircraft on the SID.

SP flew the published instrument departure to the standard expected for this block, completing the turn point and the crossing altitude after the IP's verbal prompts. Course deviation from the departure radial reached 8 degrees and was corrected with delay. Performance was at the desired code but marginal for the Training Section - unprompted recognition of track deviations is expected to improve.

SP flew the published instrument departure without IP prompting and complied with all ATC instructions. Minor track deviations of up to 6 degrees from the departure radial occurred at the turn point and were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew and executed the published instrument departure as described in the MAIP, without IP assistance and according to the Basic Control Standards. Course deviation from the departure radial was held within 4 degrees, and each deviation was corrected promptly and accurately. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the published instrument departure flawlessly, without IP assistance, with an accurate instrument cross-check maintained throughout the climb. Course deviation from the departure radial remained within 1 degree and the crossing restrictions were met with negligible error. ATC instructions were read back correctly and complied with without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect setting of the navigation source and course selector before takeoff, did not track the published departure radial after the turn point. Course deviation increased beyond 11 degrees without recognition, with the result that the IP directed the correction and flew part of the departure segment. Review of the departure setup sequence in the MAIP is required.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the departure plate, did not monitor course and climb performance during the initial climb segment. The aircraft diverged 13 degrees from the published radial and the crossing altitude was not made good, with the result that the IP intervened and re-established the SID profile.

SP, due to a lagging correction technique in which small heading changes were applied late, did not keep the aircraft on the published departure radial at the first turn point. Course deviation reached 8 degrees and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. The remainder of the SID was completed without further assistance.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the departure flown, did not initiate the turn at the specified DME and did not apply the crossing restriction from memory. Course deviation from the departure radial reached 8 degrees and the turn was started only after the IP prompted the fix, with recognition and correction achieved with delay.

SP flew the published instrument departure within the desired standards for this block, without IP intervention. Course deviation from the departure radial twice reached 7 degrees at the turn point before being self-corrected, and one ATC climb instruction required a repeated read-back. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter course control on the departure radial is expected to improve.

SP knew and executed the published instrument departure as described in the MAIP, without IP assistance and according to the Basic Control Standards. Course deviation was held within 4 degrees of the departure radial, track deviations were corrected in a timely manner, and all ATC instructions were complied with. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the published instrument departure flawlessly and without IP assistance, with an accurate instrument cross-check maintained through the climb and the turn point. Course deviation from the departure radial remained within 1 degree and the crossing restriction was met with negligible error. ATC instructions were anticipated and complied with immediately. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to sequence the navigation display to the next departure fix, did not track the published departure radial after the turn point. Course deviation exceeded 12 degrees and the aircraft was flown through the crossing fix off course, with the result that the IP directed the intercept and flew part of the departure. Review of the SID execution sequence in the MAIP is required.

SP, due to mode confusion over the selected avionics mode and what it was protecting, did not display the departure course and did not detect the divergence from the published radial. Course deviation reached 15 degrees and the ATC climb instruction was not complied with, with the result that the IP took control to re-establish the SID.

SP, due to an intercept technique that used an insufficient cut angle for the offset from the departure radial, did not regain the published course before the next fix. Course deviation stabilized at 8 degrees and was corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. Recognition of the deviation was delayed until the prompt was given.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not maintain the published departure track through the initial climb. Course deviation from the departure radial reached 8 degrees, and the correction was applied only after the IP identified the deviation verbally. The crossing restriction was subsequently met.

SP, due to a slightly late roll-out on the departure turn, did not roll out on the published radial at the turn point. Course deviation reached 7 degrees and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. ATC instructions were complied with throughout.

SP, due to inadequate workload management, with the frequency change taken inside the departure turn, did not keep the instrument cross-check on course and climb performance. Course deviation from the published radial reached 6 degrees, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, and the crossing restriction was met.

SP knew and executed the published instrument departure as described in the MAIP, without IP assistance and according to the Basic Control Standards, with course deviation held within 5 degrees of the departure radial. Corrections at the turn point, although timely, consumed most of the available tolerance on two occasions. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter margin on the departure radial is expected to improve.

SP executed the published instrument departure flawlessly, without IP assistance and within the Basic Control Standards, with an accurate cross-check maintained throughout the climb. Course deviation from the departure radial remained within 1 degree and all crossing restrictions were met with negligible error. ATC instructions were read back correctly and complied with without delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.
